message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *The RTX A6000 is available as the GPU type `nvidia-a6000`.*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # pick a zone that supports GPUs

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \ # 1 RTX A6000
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \         # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \        # official Ubuntu image repo
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \                 # size of the boot disk
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \                # SSD boot disk
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    # Install NVIDIA drivers (GPU‑optimized image already has them)
    echo "Instance ready with RTX A6000 and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS" > /var/log/startup.log'
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach the GPU (type + count) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pick the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & performance of the boot disk |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Optional script that runs after boot |

> **Tip** – If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the flags accordingly.  
> **Tip** – To see all GPU‑enabled zones, run `gcloud compute zones list --filter="supportsAccelerators:true"`.

---

## 2. REST API (curl example)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly, here’s a minimal `curl` example.  
You’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Get an access token (replace with your own method)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Define variables
PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 3️⃣  Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\necho \"Instance ready with RTX A6000 and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS\" > /var/log/startup.log"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# 4️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Explanation of the JSON payload

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type (`n1-standard-8` in this example) |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, 100 GB SSD) |
| `accelerators[0]` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script |

> **Important** – The `acceleratorType` URL must match the zone you’re using.  
> **Important** – Ensure the Compute Engine API is enabled for your project (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| Enable Compute Engine API |
| Choose a GPU‑capable zone (`supportsAccelerators:true`) |
| Pick a machine type that meets your CPU/RAM needs |
| Attach `nvidia-a6000` GPU(s) |
| Use the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family |
| Set boot disk size/type |
| (Optional) Add a startup script |

With either the `gcloud` command or the REST API call above, you’ll have a running VM that comes pre‑installed with the NVIDIA drivers needed for the RTX A6000 and is ready to run your GPU workloads on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
